evaluation.positioning_hook: After a girl’s mother is attacked by her exact double, a Maryland teen starts uncovering a town-wide secret tied to a lake creature, a hostile friend group, and a reflection that may not be his own.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The hook is easy to grasp and the teen-horror lane is commercially legible, especially with the doppelganger attack and the final lake reveal. The audience is real, but the script currently reads more niche YA horror than broad four-quadrant genre play.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The opening attack on Mrs. Bennett and the later Reddit clue make the premise understandable quickly: someone is being duplicated, and the town is hiding something aquatic. The mystery is clear, though the script is still more setup than fully articulated feature engine.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: Jer, Aria, Kylie, Noah, Tyler, and Gianna all have usable teen dynamics, but they are still mostly defined by group banter, jealousy, and reaction. The strongest character-specific tension is Kylie’s history with Gianna, yet the leads have not yet separated into fully distinctive dramatic engines.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The doppelganger-in-the-house image and the lake-creature tease give the script a fresher horror wrapper than a standard teen ensemble piece. The execution is still familiar in its school/social hierarchy material, so the originality is in the premise more than the voice.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The opening attack, Jer’s walk home, the Reddit discovery, and the pool-party confrontation keep the script moving toward a clear supernatural reveal. The middle spends a lot of time in social friction before the horror engine fully reasserts itself, which softens urgency.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The script’s strongest resonance comes from pairing teen social warfare with a body-horror identity threat, then paying it off with a creature under the water. It feels fresh enough to notice, but the deeper pattern is still recognizable genre territory rather than a fully singular construction.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: Metapeake, Maryland has a usable small-town texture: dark roads, woods, a lake-adjacent menace, and a social ecosystem where everyone knows everyone. The world is specific enough to support the mystery, but the page is still light on the town’s rules, history, and institutions.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script toggles between teen banter, jealousy comedy, and horror imagery, which gives it a recognizable YA-horror flavor. The tonal identity is not yet locked; the social scenes often play broader and more casual than the menace suggests.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: The reflection/doppelganger idea and the Reddit thread imply a larger mythology beneath the immediate attack. There are seeds of a deeper mythology, but the script has not yet revealed enough of the town’s hidden system to feel especially layered.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The friend-group dynamic is the script’s most reliable engine: Aria/Kylie, Tyler/Gianna, Jer/Noah, and the parents all create recurring friction and alliance shifts. The pool-party sequence in particular shows the ensemble can generate scenes even before the horror plot fully takes over.

lead_characters.name: Jer
lead_characters.demographics: Teen male, high-school age, likely white or unspecified, socially embedded in a close friend group.
lead_characters.hook: Jer is the anxious center of the opening mystery: a decent, slightly awkward teen who gets pulled into a nightmare when his mother is attacked by someone wearing his face. He’s observant, easily rattled, and just self-aware enough to know the world has tilted, which makes him an effective audience surrogate once the town starts lying to him.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of a young lead in a genre breakout like Jaeden Martell in It — the role asks for fear, confusion, and dry teen specificity in the same performance. It gives an actor a sustained reaction role that can turn into a full franchise face if the mythology expands.

lead_characters.name: Kylie
lead_characters.demographics: Teen female, high-school age, socially confident, emotionally guarded.
lead_characters.hook: Kylie is the sharpest social presence in the ensemble: funny, cutting, and visibly carrying old history with Gianna that turns the pool-party scene into a live wire. She reads as the friend who can joke through anything until the past hits a nerve, which gives her real scene value even before the horror escalates.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gave Sophia Lillis in It room to be funny, wounded, and commanding inside a teen ensemble. It offers an actor a memorable mix of attitude and vulnerability, especially in the confrontation and drowning sequence.

lead_characters.name: Aria
lead_characters.demographics: Teen female, high-school age, socially observant, loyal to her friends.
lead_characters.hook: Aria functions as the group’s emotional glue and social commentator, often reading the room faster than the others and backing Kylie when the tension spikes. She has a clear presence in the banter and a protective streak that makes her useful in both comedy and escalation scenes.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of ensemble-support role that lets an actor do sharp timing and reactive chemistry, similar to the friend-group energy in Booksmart. It gives a performer a chance to stand out through rhythm, not just plot weight.

lead_characters.name: Noah
lead_characters.demographics: Teen male, high-school age, friendly, socially loose, part of the core friend group.
lead_characters.hook: Noah is the easygoing comic pressure valve in the group, the one who keeps things light until the supernatural threat makes that impossible. He’s not yet deeply defined, but he helps the script feel lived-in and gives Jer someone to bounce off.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets a young actor play charm and timing in a group dynamic, like the lighter ensemble boys in Superbad. It’s a useful showcase for chemistry and comic instinct rather than heavy dramatic transformation.

lead_characters.name: Tyler
lead_characters.demographics: Teen male, high-school age, dry, defensive, romantically distracted.
lead_characters.hook: Tyler is the sarcastic one with a crush problem, which gives him a built-in friction point with both the friend group and Gianna. He’s useful because he can be annoying without being disposable, and his bluntness helps the social scenes stay active.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor do prickly teen comedy with a little romantic frustration, similar to the best supporting boys in Mean Girls. It gives a performer a chance to be memorable through attitude and timing.

lead_characters.name: Gianna
lead_characters.demographics: Teen female, high-school age, socially dominant, antagonistic, attractive to the group’s boys.
lead_characters.hook: Gianna is the social antagonist with history: she carries the old wound with Kylie and turns the pool party into a public power struggle. She’s not just mean; she’s strategic, which makes her the kind of teen rival who can anchor both social drama and horror escalation.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of a teen antagonist like Rachel McAdams in Mean Girls — the role gets to be glamorous, cutting, and controlling. It gives an actor a juicy social-villain part with real scene dominance.

lead_characters.name: Mrs. Bennett
lead_characters.demographics: Adult female, mother, suburban, protective, frightened.
lead_characters.hook: Mrs. Bennett is the first adult to experience the supernatural threat directly, and her terror gives the script its most immediate stakes. She’s a grounded parental presence whose fear is credible enough to sell the premise before the mythology opens up.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an actor a contained but intense horror showcase, like Toni Collette in Hereditary before the full collapse. It offers a strong fear-response performance and a key emotional anchor for the opening.

lead_characters.name: Mr. Bennett
lead_characters.demographics: Adult male, father, suburban, controlled, protective.
lead_characters.hook: Mr. Bennett is the stabilizing parent who tries to manage the impossible without fully understanding it. His calm under pressure helps the scene play as a family crisis rather than just a monster attack.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor play authority under strain, similar to the grounded father figures in A Quiet Place. It’s a solid supporting turn with a strong panic-to-control arc in the bathroom sequence.

lead_characters.name: Mrs. Sterling
lead_characters.demographics: Adult female, mother, suburban, casual, unaware of the danger.
lead_characters.hook: Mrs. Sterling is the ordinary adult who unknowingly confirms Jer’s alibi, which makes her a useful hinge in the mystery. She’s lightly drawn, but she helps sell the normalcy of the world before the horror starts breaking it.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a brief but functional character role that gives an actor a clean scene of confusion and concern, the kind often seen in elevated teen horror. It’s not a showcase part, but it’s a credible supporting beat.

lead_characters.name: Mr. Larsen
lead_characters.hook: Mr. Larsen is the school authority who keeps the teen social world moving with detention and classroom pressure. He’s mostly functional, but he helps establish the everyday structure the horror will later disrupt.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a straightforward authority-role part, the kind of small but useful scene work that gives an actor a clean, memorable classroom beat. It’s a utility role rather than a showcase.

casting_characteristics: One doppelganger effect requiring the same performer or matched double for Jer
Adult parents and teacher roles are supporting and age-flexible

technical.vfx_details: Reflection anomaly, doppelganger presence, shadow movement, and the final underwater creature reveal can be handled with modest digital augmentation and practical staging.
technical.sfx_needs: Water-tub attack, underwater drowning beat, practical water effects, and a creature hand reveal.

rights_flags.detail: "Party in the USA" by Miley Cyrus is explicitly used in the opening bedroom scene.
"If I Were a Boy" by Beyoncé is explicitly referenced as the next song choice.
Reddit is used as a plot-search platform in the Jer bedroom sequence.

platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model; teen horror with a mystery hook and modest effects footprint.

budget.note: Contemporary teen horror with a handful of houses, a school, streets, woods, and one pool-party set piece; the only real spend pressure is the night work and the water/creature reveal.

casting.note: The project lives or dies on finding a teen ensemble that can play banter, jealousy, and fear without flattening the horror material. Jer also needs a lead who can carry confusion and dread while staying believable as an ordinary kid.

development.note: The opening attack and final lake-creature beat are strong, but the middle leans heavily on social friction before the mythology fully asserts itself. The buyer conversation will focus on whether the teen-drama material is enough to sustain the feature between those two horror anchors.

comp_set.title: It
comp_set.why_it_comps: Teen ensemble horror with a small-town menace and a group of kids whose banter keeps the movie alive between scares.

comp_set.title: The Ring
comp_set.why_it_comps: A creeping mystery built around a disturbing image and the sense that a hidden force is moving through ordinary domestic spaces.

comp_set.title: The Faculty
comp_set.why_it_comps: High-school social dynamics collide with an invasive body-snatching threat, giving the script a familiar but marketable teen-horror lane.

comp_set.title: The Hole in the Ground
comp_set.why_it_comps: The doppelganger anxiety and parental fear around a child who may not be who they seem are the closest tonal and thematic neighbors.

audience_target.primary_audience: Teens and horror fans who like social-ensemble scares, identity horror, and small-town mystery.
audience_target.demographics: Skews 15-34, with a female-leaning teen/young-adult audience and horror-curious streamers up through their 30s.

budget_tier.note: Teen cast, contemporary locations, modest VFX, and a few night/water sequences keep this in indie feature territory.

types_of_buyers: producer-directors looking for a contained breakout feature
lane_fit.detail: This sits naturally in the lane of contemporary teen horror with a mystery spine and a contained production footprint. The social ensemble gives it enough character energy for a streamer, while the creature tease keeps it squarely in genre.

ip_potential.detail: Standalone feature at this stage; the supporting cast is functional, but no side character or world element is yet deep enough to justify a clear spinoff vector.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The opening attack is instantly legible.
strengths.what_it_means: That gives the project a fast commercial read: a buyer can understand the threat, the family stakes, and the supernatural angle in one sequence. It’s the kind of opening that helps a genre package sell on premise before the mythology is fully explained.
strengths.evidence: Mrs. Bennett is attacked by a figure that looks exactly like Jer, then the creature bolts into the woods and leaves her with finger-shaped marks.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The teen ensemble has usable chemistry.
strengths.what_it_means: The friend-group banter creates repeatable scene energy, which is valuable for both casting and audience attachment. That makes the script more attractive to buyers looking for a horror movie with personalities, not just scares.
strengths.evidence: The bedroom singalong, the lunch-table teasing, and the Tyler/Gianna/Aria jealousy triangle all play as active group scenes.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The doppelganger idea gives the horror a clean hook.
strengths.what_it_means: Identity horror is a strong commercial lane because it is easy to pitch and easy to visualize in marketing materials. The reflection beat and the Reddit clue suggest a larger mythology without requiring a huge budget.
strengths.evidence: Jer’s reflection doesn’t move with him, and the Reddit post describes a similar “someone who looked like me” attack.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The pool-party confrontation is a strong set piece.
strengths.what_it_means: It gives the script a social climax before the supernatural climax, which broadens the movie’s appeal beyond pure monster material. That kind of escalation is useful for buyers because it promises both teen-drama tension and genre payoff.
strengths.evidence: Kylie and Gianna’s confrontation escalates from old grudges to the line about being drowned in eighth grade, ending with Kylie shoved into the pool.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The lake-creature reveal lands as a clean button.
strengths.what_it_means: The final underwater hand is a simple, marketable image that can anchor trailers and poster art without requiring a giant effects spend. It also confirms the script’s creature-mystery lane in a way that feels like a real turn, not just a tease.
strengths.evidence: After Kylie sinks, a long blue-green hand reaches up from beneath the water and the scene cuts to black.

whats_special.headline: This has the bones of a sellable teen-horror package: a clean supernatural hook, a social ensemble that can carry scenes, and a contained contemporary footprint that keeps the economics friendly. The opening attack and pool-party climax give a buyer two strong trailer moments, while the doppelganger/lake-creature mythology points to a marketable mystery lane for streaming or indie genre buyers.

items.area: The middle leans on social friction.
items.detail: Once the Bennett attack lands, the script spends a long stretch on school banter, jealousy, and relationship triangulation before the horror engine fully reasserts itself. That is workable for a teen-horror audience, but it makes the feature feel more like setup than escalation for a significant portion of the runtime.

items.area: Jer is still more witness than driver.
items.detail: He gets the opening nightmare, the Reddit clue, and the final unease, but most of the active social energy belongs to Kylie, Aria, Tyler, and Gianna. Buyers will notice that the nominal lead is not yet the most dramatic person in the room, which can flatten the center of gravity.

items.area: The mythology is still thin on rules.
items.detail: The reflection anomaly, the doppelganger attack, the Reddit post, and the lake hand all point in the same direction, but the script has not yet defined what the creature is, how it operates, or why this town is vulnerable. That keeps the hook intriguing, but it also means the buyer is evaluating promise more than payoff.

"Party in the USA" and "If I Were a Boy" are both explicitly named in the opening bedroom scene, and Reddit is used as a plot-search platform. The music items are the only real legal line items, but they are still real budget and clearance conversations.

issues.headline: The main friction is structural rather than conceptual: the opening and ending are strong, but the script spends a lot of the middle in teen-social mode before the horror mythology takes over. Buyers will also clock that Jer is not yet the most forceful engine on the page, so the project is currently being sold more on premise and ensemble energy than on a fully commanding lead.
